{{Short description|British mathematician (1943–2018)}}
{{Use British English|date=April 2018}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2018}}
'''Frederick Bernard de Neumann''' (known in [[Austria]] and [[Germany]] as ''Bernhard von Neumann''; (15 December 1943 – 18 April 2018<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/notice/3175529 |title=Frederick De Neumann |website=www.thegazette.co.uk |access-date=2019-10-14}}</ref>) was a [[British people|British]] [[mathematician]], [[computer scientist]], [[inventor]], and [[naval history|naval historian]].

He was educated at the [[Royal Hospital School]] and [[Birmingham University]], and was Professor of Mathematics at [[City St George's, University of London|The City University]].

He was a descendant of Johann Andreas von Neumann, nobleman of the [[Holy Roman Empire]], [[Vienna]], 29 March 1797, and of Johann Heinrich von Neumann, nobleman of the [[Kingdom of Bavaria]], [[Munich]], 20 January 1824.
